translations.text: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in the prophets: “Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you.”
“The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”
And John was baptizing in the wilderness and preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
The whole land of Judea and all the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and they were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
John wore camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
He preached and said, “Someone stronger than I is coming after me. I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the straps of his sandals.”
“I baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
Immediately, as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn open and the Spirit of God descending on him like a dove.
A voice came from heaven and said, “You are my beloved Son; I am pleased with you.”
And immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
He was there for forty days, tempted by Satan. He was with the wild beasts, and the angels served him.
After John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of God.
He said, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent and believe in the gospel.”
As he walked along the shore of the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, Simon’s brother, casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
Going a little farther from there, he saw James, the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who were also in the boat, mending their nets.
He called them, and immediately they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and followed him.
They entered Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath he entered the synagogue and taught them.
They were astonished at his teaching, because he taught them as one with authority, and not like the scribes.
In their synagogue there was a man with an unclean spirit in him, who cried out and said,
“Leave us alone! What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? We know who you are: the Holy One of God.”
Jesus rebuked him and said, “Be silent and come out of him!”
The unclean spirit convulsed him, cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
They were all amazed, so that they whispered to one another and said, “What is this new teaching? With authority he even rebukes unclean spirits, and they obey him!”
And news of him spread throughout the whole region of Galilee.
And immediately, leaving the synagogue, he came to the house of Simon and Andrew, together with James and John.
Now Simon’s mother-in-law lay sick with a fever, and they immediately told him about her.
And he approached her, took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served them.
And when evening came, at sunset, they brought to him all who were sick and possessed by demons.
And the whole city was gathered at the door.
And he healed many who were sick with various diseases and cast out many demons. He did not allow the demons to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.
And at dawn, early in the morning, he rose, went out, and departed to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
And Simon and those who were with him went after him.
And when they found him, they said to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
And he said to them, “Come, let us go to the other nearby towns, so that I may preach there too, for this is precisely why I have come.”
He preached in their congregations among all the Galileans and drove out demons.
A leper came to him, begged him, knelt down, and said, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
But Jesus, moved with compassion, stretched out his hand, came near him, and said to him, “I am willing. Be cleansed.”
And when he said this to him, the leprosy immediately left him, and he was cleansed.
And he sternly warned him, immediately sent him away, and said to him,
“Be careful not to say anything to anyone. Instead, go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing the offering that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

But he went out and began to proclaim it widely and spread the news, so that Jesus could no longer enter a city openly. Instead, he stayed outside in deserted places, and people came to him from every direction.
And after some days he entered Capernaum again.
It became known that he was in the house, and many gathered, so that there was no more room, not even at the door. And he spoke the word to them.
And they came to him, bringing a paralyzed man carried by four people.
And when they could not get near him because of the crowd, they tore open the roof where Jesus was. Having opened the ceiling, they lowered the bed on which the paralyzed man lay.
And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “Son, let your sins be forgiven.”
Some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts.
“Why does this man speak blasphemies? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
And Jesus knew in his spirit that they were thinking this way in their hearts, and he said, “Why do you think these things in your hearts?”
“Which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Let your sins be forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, take your bed, and go to your house’?”
“But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man—
I say to you, get up, take your mat, and go to your house.
He got up, immediately took his mat, and went out in front of everyone. They were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this.”
He went out again to the seashore, and all the people came to him, and he taught them.
As he passed by, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.
As he was reclining at the table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many who followed him.
When the scribes and Pharisees saw that he was eating with tax collectors and sinners, they said to his disciples, “Why does he eat and drink with sinners and tax collectors?”
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “The healthy have no need of a doctor, but the sick do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. They came and said to him, “Why do John’s disciples and the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?”
Jesus said to them, “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast on that day.
No one sews a new, unshrunk patch onto an old garment. Otherwise, the new patch pulls away from the old cloth, and the tear becomes even worse.
No one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the wine bursts the wineskins, the wine spills out, and the wineskins are ruined. Instead, new wine must be put into new wineskins.”
He was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to pluck heads of grain and eat them as they walked.
The Pharisees said to him, “Look at what your disciples are doing on the Sabbath, which is not lawful.”
Jesus said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and was hungry, he and those who were with him?
How he entered the house of God when Abiathar was high priest, ate the bread of the Presence, and also gave it to those who were with him, although only the priests were permitted to eat it?”
He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for humankind, not humankind for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
He entered the synagogue again, and a man was there whose hand was withered.
They watched him to see whether he would heal the man on the Sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
He said to the man whose hand was withered, “Get up and come into the middle.”
He said to them, “What is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?” But they remained silent.
Jesus looked around at them with anger, grieved at the blindness of their hearts, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
The Pharisees went out and immediately took counsel with the Herodians about how to destroy him.
Jesus went to the seashore with his disciples, and a large crowd from Galilee and Judea followed him.
And a large crowd from Jerusalem, from beyond the Jordan, and from Tyre and Sidon came to him when they heard about all that he was doing.
And he told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush him.
For he had healed many, so that those who had ailments came crowding around him to get close to him.
And whenever the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him, cried out, and said,
“You are the Son of God.” And he sternly warned them not to make him known.
He goes up the mountain and calls to himself those he wanted, and they went to him.
And he appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out by him to preach
and to have authority to heal diseases and cast out demons.
And he gave Simon the name Peter.
And to James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James he gave the name Boanerges, which means Sons of Thunder.
And Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew the tax collector, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
They come into a house, and the crowd gathers with them again, so that they do not even have time to eat bread.
And when his family heard this, they went out to seize him, for they thought he was out of his mind.
And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem said, “Beelzebul is in him, and he casts out demons by the ruler of the demons.”
And he called them to him and spoke to them in parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a household is divided against itself, that household cannot stand.
And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but has come to an end.
But no one can enter a strong man’s house and plunder his possessions unless he first binds the strong man. Then he will plunder his house.
Truly I tell you, all sins will be forgiven the children of humankind, and all blasphemies, however much they blaspheme.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never have forgiveness, but will be guilty of eternal sins.”
For they were saying, “An unclean spirit is in him.”
His brothers and his mother come, and standing outside, they sent word and called him.
And a crowd was sitting around him there. When they said to him, “Look, your mother and your brothers are outside looking for you,”
he answered them and said, “Who is my mother, or who are my brothers?”
He looked around at his disciples who were sitting around him and said, “Here are my mother and my brothers.”
For whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.
Again he began to teach by the sea, and large crowds gathered around him, so that he got into a boat and sat in it on the sea, while all the people were on the land along the shore.
He taught them many things in parables and said to them in his teaching:
Listen! A sower went out to sow.
As he sowed, some seed fell beside the road, and a bird came and ate it.
Other seed fell on rocky ground, where there was not much soil, and it sprang up immediately because there was no moisture in the soil.
When the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no roots, it withered.
Other seed fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
Other seed fell on good soil, sprang up, grew, and yielded fruit, producing thirty, sixty, and a hundred times what was sown.
And he said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.”
When he was alone, those around him, together with the disciples, asked him about the parables.
He said to them, “You have been given knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but for those outside, everything is in parables,
so that they may look and look but not see, and listen and listen but not understand, lest they ever turn back and be forgiven.”
He said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? How, then, will you understand all the parables?
The sower sows the word.
These are the ones beside the road, where the word is sown: when they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word sown in their hearts.
These are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy,
but because they have no root in themselves, they last only a short time. Then, when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately fall away.
Those sown among the thorns are the ones who hear the word,
but the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of wealth enter in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
These are the ones sown on good soil: they hear the word, accept it, and bear fruit, thirty, sixty, and a hundred times what was sown.”
He said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under a basket or under a bed? Is it not to be put on a lampstand?
For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, and nothing has been kept secret that will not come to light.
If anyone has ears to hear, let them hear.”
He said to them, “Pay attention to what you hear, and more will be given to you who hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you.
Whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away from them.”
And he said, “The kingdom of God is like this: a man scatters seed on the ground,
and sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how.
For the earth produces fruit by itself: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
But when it yields its fruit, he immediately sends in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
He said, “To what shall we compare the kingdom of God, or with what parable shall we describe it?”
“Like a mustard seed, which, when sown in the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on earth,
yet when it is sown, it sprouts and becomes larger than all the garden plants and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can dwell in its shade.”
And with such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
He spoke nothing to them without a parable, but privately he explained everything to his disciples.
And on that day, when evening came, he said to them, “Come, let us cross to the other side.”
They leave the crowd and take him along with the boat, and also the other boats that were with him.
And a great windstorm arose, and the waves poured into the boat, so that it was almost full.
But he was sleeping in the stern of the boat on a cushion. They woke him and said, “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”
And he awoke, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be still! Be silent!” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them, “Why are you so fainthearted? Do you still have no faith?” And they were greatly afraid and said to one another, “Who can this be, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
And he came to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gergesenes.
And as he came out of the boat, a man possessed by an unclean spirit met him from among the tombs.
He made his home among the tombs, and no one could bind him anymore, even with chains.
For he had often been bound with shackles and chains, but he had torn apart the chains and broken the shackles, and no one could subdue him.
For continually, night and day, he cried out among the tombs and in the mountains and struck himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before him.
He cried out with a loud voice and said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore you by God, do not torment me!”
For he was saying to him, “Come out of that man, you unclean spirit!”
And he asked him, “What is your name?” And he said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”
And they begged him earnestly not to send them out of the country.
And there by the mountain was a large herd of pigs feeding.
All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs so that we may enter them.”

He gave them permission, and when the unclean spirits came out, they entered the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea. There were about two thousand of them, and they drowned in the sea.
The swineherds fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside, and people came out to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man sitting there, clothed and in his right mind—the man who had had the legion—and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the demon-possessed man and what had happened to the pigs.
They began to beg him to leave their territory.
As he got into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed begged him to let him be with him.
Jesus did not allow him, but said to him, “Go home to your family and tell them all that the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you.”
He went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis all that Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
When Jesus crossed again to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him, and he was by the seashore.
One of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came, and when he saw him, he fell at his feet.
He begged him earnestly, saying that his daughter was near death and that he should come and lay his hand on her so that she might be healed and live.
He went with him, and a large crowd followed him and pressed against him.
There was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She had suffered greatly under many physicians and had spent all she had, but had gained no benefit and had instead grown worse.
When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and took hold of his clothing.
For she thought to herself, “If I only touch his clothing, I will be healed.”
Immediately the source of her bleeding dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been healed of her affliction.
Immediately Jesus knew within himself that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched my clothing?”
His disciples said to him, “You see that the crowd is pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched my clothing?’”
He looked around to see who had done this.
The woman, frightened and trembling because of what she had done in secret, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell before him and told him the whole truth.
Jesus said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be healed of your affliction.”
While he was still speaking, some people came from the synagogue leader’s house and said, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any further?”
But when Jesus heard what was said, he said to the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid; only believe.”
He allowed no one to go with him except Peter, James, and John, the brother of James.
He comes to the house of the synagogue leader and sees a great commotion, with people weeping and crying out loudly.
He goes inside and says to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child is not dead but sleeping.”
They laughed at him. But he put everyone outside, took with him the child's father and mother and those who were with him, and went in where the child lay.
Taking the child by the hand, he says to her, “Talitha koumi,” which means, “Girl, I say to you, get up.”
Immediately the girl got up and walked, for she was about twelve years old. They were greatly astonished.
He strictly ordered them not to let anyone know about this, and told them to give her something to eat.
He left there and came to his own region, and his disciples followed him.

On the Sabbath he began teaching in the synagogue. Many who heard him were astonished at his teaching and said, “Where did he get these things? What is this wisdom given to him, that such miracles should be performed by his hands?”
“Is this not the young carpenter and the son of Mary, the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
Jesus says to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his own region, among his relatives, and in his own house.”
He could not perform any miracle there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
He marveled at their unbelief. And he went around the surrounding districts, teaching.
He called the twelve to him and began sending them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff: no bag, no bread, and no copper money in their belts.
They were to wear sandals, but he said, “Do not wear two tunics.”
He said to them, “Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that place.”
“Wherever people do not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave there, as a testimony against them.”
They went out and preached that people should repent.
They cast out many demons, anointed many sick people with oil, and healed them.
King Herod heard about him, for his name had become well known. He said, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and that is why miracles are performed through him.”
Others said, “He is Elijah,” while still others said, “He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.”
When Herod heard this, he said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
For Herod himself had sent men to seize John, bind him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, whom he had married.
For John had been saying to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.”
Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
For Herod feared John, because he knew him to be a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he listened to him gladly.
An opportune day came when Herod gave a dinner on his birthday for his officials, military commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.
When the daughter of Herodias came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those dining with him. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
He swore to her many times, “Whatever you ask me for, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”
She went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” She said, “The head of John the Baptist.”
She immediately hurried back in to the king and said, “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter right now.”
The king was deeply grieved, but because of his oaths and his dinner guests, he did not want to refuse her.
The king immediately sent an executioner and ordered him to bring John's head. He went and beheaded him in prison.
He brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl took it and gave it to her mother.
When his disciples heard about it, they came, took his body, and laid it in a tomb.
The apostles gathered around Jesus and told him everything they had done and taught.
Jesus said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
They went away by boat to a deserted place by themselves.
Many saw them leaving and recognized them. They hurried there together on foot from all the towns and came near them.
When he came out, he saw a large crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. He began to teach them at length.
When much time had passed, his disciples came to him and said, “This is a deserted place, and there is still daylight.
Send these people away so that they can go to the surrounding farms and villages and buy themselves something to eat, because they have nothing to eat here.”
He answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?”
He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” When they found out, they said to him, “Five, and two fish.”
He ordered them to have everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.
They sat down in groups, some of a hundred and some of fifty.
Taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, blessed and broke the loaves, and gave them to the disciples to set before the people. He also divided the two fish among them all.
They ate and were satisfied.
They gathered twelve baskets full of leftover pieces, including some of the fish.
Those who ate were about five thousand men.
Immediately he urged the disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he dismissed the crowd.
After taking leave of them, he went up the mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was on land.
He saw them struggling to row, because the wind was against them. During the fourth watch of the night, he came toward them, walking on the sea, and intended to pass by them.
When they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost and cried out.
For they all saw him and were troubled. Immediately he spoke to them and said, “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
He got into the boat with them, and the wind stopped. They were even more bewildered in their minds and were greatly amazed.
For they had not understood about the bread either, because their hearts were dull.
When they crossed to the other side, they came to the land of Gennesaret.
As soon as they got out of the boat, the men of that place recognized him.
They ran here and there throughout the whole region and began bringing the sick on beds wherever they heard he was.
Wherever he entered villages, cities, or farms, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged him to let them touch even the fringe of his clothing. Everyone who touched it was healed.
The Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him.
When they saw some of his disciples eating bread with unclean hands, that is, unwashed hands, they criticized them.
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat bread unless they wash their hands thoroughly, because they hold to the tradition of the elders.

When they come from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they first wash themselves. There are also many other practices they have received and observe: the washing of cups, pitchers, copper vessels, and beds.
Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, “Why do your disciples not follow the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unclean hands?”
He answered and said to them, “Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as he said: ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far away from me.’”
They worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines commandments given by human beings.
“You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.”
He said to them, “You are very good at rejecting the commandment of God so that you may establish your own tradition.”
“For Moses says, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil of father or mother must be put to death.’”
“But you say, ‘If someone says to his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might receive from me is Corban”—that is, an offering—’”
“then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother.”
“You dishonor the word of God through your tradition, which you have handed down, and you do many other things like this.”
He called the whole crowd to him and said to them, “Listen to me, all of you, and understand.”
Nothing that enters a person from outside can defile them. Rather, what comes out of a person is what defiles them.
Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
When he entered a house away from the crowd, his disciples asked him about the parable.
And he said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not understand that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile them,
because it does not enter their heart but their stomach, and then passes out, cleansing all foods?”
And he said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles them.
For from within, from people’s hearts, come evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual immoralities,
thefts, murders, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, lust, envy, blasphemy, arrogance, and foolishness.
All these evil things come from within and defile a person.”
And he left that place and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon. He entered a house and did not want anyone to know, but he could not remain hidden.
A woman whose daughter was afflicted by an unclean spirit heard about him, came, and fell down before him.
The woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician by birth, and she begged him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
And Jesus said to her, “Let the children be satisfied first, for it is not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
She answered and said, “Lord, even the dogs feed on the crumbs from the children’s table.”
And he said to her, “Because of that answer, go. The demon has left your daughter.”
She went home and found that the demon had left and that her daughter was lying on the bed.
He left the region of Tyre and Sidon again and came to the shore of the Sea of Galilee, within the region of the Decapolis.
They brought before him a man who was deaf and mute and begged him to lay his hand on him.
He took him aside, away from the crowd, put his fingers into his ears, spat there, and took hold of his tongue.
He looked up to heaven, sighed, and said, “Ephphatha,” which means, “Be opened.”
And immediately his ears were opened, the bonds of his tongue were loosened, and he spoke clearly.
And he commanded them not to tell anyone. But the more he commanded them, the more they proclaimed it.
And they were astonished beyond measure and said, “He has done everything well. He makes the deaf hear and those unable to speak talk.”
In those days there was again a large crowd, and they had nothing to eat. He called his disciples and said to them,
“I have compassion for this crowd, because they have now been with me for three days and have nothing to eat.
And if I send them home hungry, they will faint on the way, because some of them have come from far away.”
His disciples answered him, “Where can you get enough bread to satisfy these people here in the wilderness?”
And he asked them, “How many loaves of bread do you have?” And they said, “Seven.”
And he ordered the crowd to sit down on the ground. He took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to serve, and they served them to the crowd.
They also had a few fish, and he blessed these too and ordered them to be served.
They ate and were satisfied, and they picked up seven baskets of leftover pieces.
There were about four thousand who ate, and he sent them away.
Immediately he got into the boat with his disciples and came to the region of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came and began to argue with him, asking him for a sign from heaven to test him.
He became indignant in his spirit and said, “Why does this generation ask for a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
He left them, got into the boat again, and went to the other side.
They had forgotten to bring bread and had only one loaf with them in the boat.
He warned them, saying, “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of the Herodians.”
They reasoned with one another and said, “It is because we have no bread.”
Jesus knew and said to them, “Why are you thinking in your hearts, you of little faith, that you have no bread? Do you still not understand or remember? Are your hearts stupefied?
You have eyes, but do you not see? You have ears, but do you not hear? Do you still not understand or remember?
When [?] the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you pick up?” They said to him, “Twelve.”
“And when [?] the seven loaves among the four thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you pick up?” They said, “Seven.”
He said to them, “Then how is it that you do not understand?”
They came to Bethsaida, and people brought a blind man before him and begged him to touch him.
He took the blind man by the hand and led him outside the village. He spat into his eyes, laid his hand on him, and asked him whether he could see anything.
He opened his eyes and said, “I see people, for they walk about like trees.”
Again he laid his hands on his eyes. He opened his eyes and could see; he was healed and saw everything clearly.
He sent him home and said, “Do not enter the village, but go home; and when you enter the village, do not tell anyone in the village.”
Jesus went out with his disciples to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do people say I am?”
They answered him, “John the Baptist; others say Elijah, and others, one of the prophets.”
He said to them, “But who do you say I am?” Peter answered him, “You are the Christ.”
He sternly warned them not to tell anyone about him.
He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, die, and rise on the third day.
He spoke openly about this, and Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
He turned, saw his disciples, rebuked Peter, and said, “Get behind me, Satan, for you are not thinking about the things of God but the things of people.”
He called the crowd to him along with his disciples and said to them, “If anyone wants to follow me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.”
“For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for the sake of the gospel will save it.”
“What does it profit a person to gain the whole world and lose his own life?”
“For what can a person give in exchange for his life?”
“For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father and of the holy angels.”
He said to them, “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God come with power.”
After six days, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him and led them up a high mountain by themselves. He was transfigured before them.
His clothes became dazzling and exceedingly white, whiter than any launderer on earth could make them.
Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were speaking with Jesus.
Peter spoke up and said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
For he did not know what to say, because they were terrified.
A cloud overshadowed them, and a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
Suddenly, when they looked around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus alone.
As they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
They kept the saying in mind and discussed with one another what rising from the dead might mean.
They asked him, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
He answered them, “Elijah comes first and restores everything. Yet how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer many things and be treated with contempt?”
But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.
When they came to the disciples, they saw a crowd around them and the scribes arguing with them.
Immediately, when the whole crowd saw him, they were amazed and ran to greet him.
He asked them, “What were you arguing about with them?”
Someone from the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a spirit that makes him unable to speak.”
“Wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and wastes away. I told your disciples to cast it out, but they could not cast it out.”
He answered them, “O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I put up with you? Bring him to me.”
They brought him to Jesus. When the spirit saw him, it immediately threw the boy into convulsions. He fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
He asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been happening to him?” He said, “Since childhood.”
It often throws him into fire and into water to destroy him. Now, if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us, Lord.
And Jesus said to him, “You said, ‘If you can.’ Everything is possible for the one who believes.”
Immediately the child’s father cried out and said, “I believe! Help my unbelief!”
When Jesus saw that the crowd was gathering, he rebuked the unclean spirit and said, “Mute and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again.”
It cried out, convulsed him violently, and came out. The boy became like a dead person, so that many even said, “He is dead.”
But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him up, and he stood up.
When he entered the house, the disciples asked him privately, “Why could we not cast it out?”
He said to them, “This kind cannot come out by anything except fasting and prayer.”
They left that place and passed among the Galileans, and he did not want anyone to know.
For he was teaching his disciples and saying to them, “The Son of Man will be handed over into human hands, and they will kill him. When he is killed, he will rise on the third day.”
They did not understand the saying and were afraid to ask him.
He came to Capernaum, and when he entered the house, he asked them, “What were you arguing about with one another on the road?”
But they remained silent, because on the road they had been arguing with one another about who was the greatest.
He sat down, called the twelve, and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be the least of all and the servant of all.”
He took a child and placed him among them. Taking him into his arms, he said to them:
“Whoever receives one of these children in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives not me but the one who sent me.”
John answered him and said, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and he did not follow us, so we stopped him.”
He said, “Do not stop him, for no one who performs miracles in my name can speak evil of me.”
“For whoever is not against us is on our side.”
“And whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in this name, because you belong to Christ, truly I tell you, will not lose his reward.”
“And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a donkey’s millstone were put around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.”
“And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter eternal life maimed than to have two hands and go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.”
“And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter eternal life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into Gehenna.”
“And if your eye causes you to stumble, remove it. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,”
“where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.”
“For everything will be salted with fire.”
Salt is good, but if the salt loses its flavor, with what will it be seasoned? So keep salt in yourselves, and make peace with one another.
He left there and came to the region of Judea beyond the Jordan. The crowd again came flocking to him, and, as was his custom, he taught them again.
The Pharisees approached and, to test him, asked him, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his [?]?”
He answered them and said, “What did Moses command you?”
They said, “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and send her away.”
Jesus answered and said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart he wrote that commandment for you.
But from the beginning of creation, God made them male and female, and he says,
‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and follow his wife,
and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Therefore, let no one separate what God has joined together.”
In the house, the disciples asked him again about the same thing.
He said to them, “If a man divorces his wife and marries another, he commits adultery.
And if a woman leaves her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”
They were bringing children to him so that he would lay his hand on them, but the disciples rebuked those who brought them.
When Jesus saw this, he became angry, rebuked them, and said, “Let the children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it.”
He took them in his arms, laid his hand on them, and blessed them.
As he was leaving there to go on his way, a rich man ran up, knelt down, and asked him, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not bear false witness. Honor your father and mother.’”
He answered and said to him, “Teacher, I have done all these things since my childhood. What do I still lack?”

Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “You lack one thing. If you want to be perfect, go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then take up the cross and come, follow me.”
His face fell at these words, and he went away sorrowful, because he had many possessions.
Jesus looked around and said to the disciples, “How hard it is for those who have possessions to enter the kingdom of God!”
The disciples were astonished at his words. But Jesus answered them again and said, “Children, how hard it is for those who trust in possessions to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a rope to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
They were even more astonished and said to one another, “Then who can be saved?”
Jesus looked at them and said, “For human beings this is impossible, but not for God.”
Peter began to say to him, “Look, we have left everything and followed you.”
Jesus answered and said, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left a house or brothers or sisters or father or mother or children or fields for my sake or for the sake of the gospel
who will not receive a hundred times as much now in this time—houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions—and eternal life in the world to come.
For many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

They were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them. Those following him were amazed and afraid. Taking the twelve aside again, he began to tell them what would happen to him,
saying, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles.
They will mock him, beat him, spit on him, and kill him, and on the third day he will rise.”
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to him and said, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you.”
He said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said to him, “Grant us to sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your glory.”
Jesus answered and said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am going to be baptized?”
They said to him, “We can.” Jesus said to them, “You will drink the cup that I am going to drink, and you will be baptized with the baptism with which I am going to be baptized.
But to grant seats at my right and at my left is not mine to give; they are for those for whom they have been prepared.”
When the ten heard this, they began to be angry with James and John.
Jesus called them to him and said to them, “You know that those who are called rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great men exercise authority over them.
It must not be so among you. Instead, whoever among you wants to become great must be your servant,
and whoever among you wants to be first must be everyone's slave.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom in exchange for many.”
They came to Jericho. As he was leaving Jericho with his disciples and large crowds, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out and say, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Many rebuked him, telling him to be silent, but he cried out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and ordered them to call him. They called the blind man and said to him, “Take courage! Get up; he is calling you.”
He threw off his cloak, got up, and came to Jesus.
Jesus answered him and said, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “Rabboni, let me regain my sight.”
Jesus said to him, “Go; your faith has made you well.” Immediately he regained his sight and followed him on the road.
When they drew near Jerusalem, at Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, he sends two of the disciples.
And he said to them, “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately as you enter it, you will find a colt tied up, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.”
And if anyone says to you, “Why are you untying that colt?” say, “Its Lord needs it, and he will send it here immediately.”
They went and found the colt tied outside at a door in the street, and they untied it.
Some of those standing there said to them, “What are you doing, untying that colt?”
They answered them as Jesus had told them, and they let them go.
They brought the colt to Jesus and put garments on it, and he sat on it.
Many spread their garments on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and scattered them along the road.
Those going ahead and those following shouted and said, “Hosanna to the Most High! Blessed are you who come in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. He looked around at everything, and since it was already late, he went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, he was hungry.
He saw a fig tree in leaf from a distance and went to see whether he could find anything on it. When he came to it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not yet the season for figs.
He said to it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” And his disciples heard him.

They came to Jerusalem, and he entered the temple and began driving out the sellers and buyers who were in the temple. He scattered the money changers’ tables and overturned the seats of those selling doves.
He would not allow anyone to carry any vessel through the temple.
He taught them and said, “It is written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations,’ but you have made it a den of robbers.”
The chief priests and scribes heard this and sought a way to destroy him. But they feared him, because all the people were astonished at his teaching.
When evening came, they went outside the city.
As they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots.
Peter remembered and said to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed has withered.”
Jesus answered and said to them, “If you have faith in God.”
“Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen, will have whatever he says.
Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, if you believe that you will receive it, it will be yours.
And whenever you stand praying, forgive if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses.
For if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive you your trespasses.”
They came again to Jerusalem, and as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, scribes, and elders came to him.
They said to him, “By what authority do you do these things, and who gave you this authority?”
Jesus answered them, “I too will ask you one question. Give me an answer, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.”
“Was John’s baptism from heaven or from human beings? Give me an answer.”
They reasoned with one another and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Then why did you not believe him?’”
“But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ we fear the people, because everyone knew that John was a prophet.”
They answered Jesus, “We do not know.” Jesus answered them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
And he began to speak to them in parables, saying, “A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a pit for a winepress, built a tower, leased it to tenants, and went to a foreign country.”
At the proper time he sent a servant to the tenant farmers to receive from them some of the fruit of the vineyard.
They seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
Again he sent another servant to them. They wounded him in the head and sent him away dishonored.
Again he sent another, and they killed him. He sent many others; some they beat, and some they killed.
He still had one beloved son. He sent him to them last, saying, “Perhaps they will respect this son of mine.”
But when the tenant farmers saw him coming, they said to one another, “This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.”
They seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
“Now what will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenant farmers and put the vineyard into the hands of others.”
“Have you not read this scripture: ‘The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone;
this came from the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes’?”
They sought to seize him, but they feared the people, because they realized that he had spoken the parable against them. So they left him and went away.
They sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to him to trap him in his words.

They came and questioned him deceitfully, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and do not concern yourself with anyone’s status, because you do not judge people by appearances, but teach the way of God truthfully. Now tell us: Is it lawful to pay tax to Caesar or not? Should we pay or should we not pay?”
Jesus knew their hypocrisy and said to them, “Why are you testing me, hypocrites? Bring me a denarius so that I may see it.”
They brought one, and he said to them, “Whose image is this, and whose inscription?” They said to him, “Caesar’s.”
Jesus answered them, “Go, give Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and God what belongs to God.” And they were amazed at him.
The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to him and questioned him, saying:
“Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone’s brother dies and leaves a wife but leaves no child, his brother should marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.”
“Now there were seven brothers among us. The first married a woman and died, leaving no offspring.”
“The second married the same woman and died, and he too left no offspring. Likewise, the third married the same woman.”
“All seven left no offspring. After them all, the woman also died.”
“Now, in the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For all seven had married her.”
Jesus answered them, “Is this not why you are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, men do not take wives, nor do women become wives of men, but they are like the angels in heaven.

But concerning the resurrection of the dead, that they rise, have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God said to him, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are therefore greatly mistaken.”
One of the scribes came forward and heard them debating. When he saw that Jesus had answered them well, he asked him, “Which commandment is first?”
Jesus said to him, “The first of all is: ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
The second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
The scribe said to him, “Well said, Teacher. You have truly said that God is one and that there is no other besides him.”
“And to love him with all one's heart, with all one's strength, and with all one's mind, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is more than burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
When Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to ask him anything more.
While teaching in the temple, Jesus said, “How do the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
David himself says through the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.’
If David himself calls him Lord, how can he be his son?” And the large crowd listened to him gladly.
In his teaching he said, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in showy clothing and seek greetings of honor in the marketplaces,
the foremost seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at dinners.
They devour widows’ houses and make long prayers as a pretense. They will receive an even greater condemnation.”
Jesus was opposite the treasury, watching how the crowd put copper coins into it. Many rich people put in large amounts.
A widow came and put in two small coins, worth one quadrans.
He called his disciples to him and said to them, “Truly I tell you, that poor widow put in more than all those who put money into the treasury.
For they all contributed from their surplus, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had, her entire livelihood.”
As he was leaving the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, look at these magnificent stones and buildings!”
Jesus answered him, “Do you see all these buildings? Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left upon another that will not be torn down.”
As he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him privately,
“Tell us, when will this happen, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be fulfilled?”
Jesus answered them, “Be on your guard so that no one deceives you.”
For many will come in my name and say, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will lead many astray.
But when you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed, for these things must happen, but the end is not yet.

For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in various places, famines, slaughters, and disturbances. But all these things are the beginning of birth pains.
And they will hand you yourselves over to courts, and you will be tortured in assemblies, and you will stand before judges and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to all the nations.
But first this gospel must be preached.

But when they take you away to hand you over, do not worry beforehand or consider what you will say. Instead, say whatever is given to you at that hour, for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
Brother will hand brother over to death, and a father his child, and children will rise against their parents and kill them.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name, but whoever endures to the end will be saved.
And when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be—let the reader understand—then those who are in Judea must flee to the mountains.
And whoever is on the housetop must not go down into the house or enter to take anything from his house.
And whoever is in the field must not turn back to take his clothes.
But woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days!
Pray that this does not happen in winter.
Those days will be days of distress such as has never occurred from the beginning of creation until now, and will never occur again.
And if God had not shortened those days for the sake of his chosen ones, no one would survive. But for the sake of the chosen ones whom he chose, he shortened those days.
Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There he is!’ do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and perform signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
But be on your guard. Look, I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that distress, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
And the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming with clouds, with great power and glory.
And then he will send his angels and gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven.
But learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branches gradually become tender and leaves sprout on it, you know that summer is near.
Likewise, when you see all these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But no one knows about that day and hour—not the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
Be on your guard, [?], and remain in prayer, for you do not know when the time will come.
It is like a man going to a foreign country who leaves his house, gives his servants authority, assigns each his work, and commands the doorkeeper to stay awake.
So stay awake, for you do not know when the master of the house will come—in the evening, at midnight, at cockcrow, or in the morning.
Otherwise, he may come suddenly and find you asleep.
But what I say to you, I say to everyone: Stay awake.
The Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away. The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to seize him by deceit and kill him.
But they were saying, “Not here during the festival, so that there will not be an uproar among the people.”
While he was reclining at the table in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, a woman came with a flask of very costly, fine nard oil. She broke the flask and poured it over his head.
The disciples were indignant and said, “Why this waste of oil?”
“This oil could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” And they were very angry with her.
Jesus said to them, “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has done a good deed for me.”
“You always have the poor with you, and whenever you wish, you can do good to them. But you do not always have me with you.”
“She did what she could. She perfumed my body beforehand as a sign of its burial.”
“Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what she has done will also be told in remembrance of her.”
Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to hand him over to them.
When they heard this, they rejoiced and promised to give him money. And he looked for a convenient opportunity to hand him over.
On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when they slaughtered the Passover lamb, his disciples said to him, “Where do you want us to go and make preparations for you to eat the Passover?”
He sent two of his disciples and said to them, “Go into the city, and when you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water on his shoulder will meet you. Follow him.”
“Whatever house he enters, say to the owner of the house, ‘The Teacher says: Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’”
“He will show you a large upstairs room, furnished. Make preparations for us there.”
His disciples went to make preparations. They came into the city and found everything as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When evening came, he arrived with the Twelve.
When they had reclined at the table and were still eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me—one who is eating with me.”
And they began to be sorrowful and to say to him one by one, “Is it I?” And another said, “Is it I?”
He answered and said to them, “It is one of the Twelve, the one who dipped with me into the dish.”
“But the Son of Man goes as it is written about him. Yet woe to that man through whose hands the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had never been born.”
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “Take it; this is my body.”
Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
He said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many.
Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
After giving thanks, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
But after my resurrection, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter answered and said to him, “Even if everyone falls away, I will not.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
But Peter insisted all the more, saying, “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” And they all said the same.
They came to a village called Gethsemane, and he said to the disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
He took Peter, James, and John with him and began to be sorrowful and distressed.
Then he said to them, “My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
Going a little farther, he fell facedown on the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.
He said, “Abba, Father, all things are possible for you. Take this cup away from me, but not as I will, but as you will.”
He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for one hour?
Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again he went away and prayed, saying the same words.
He returned once more and found them asleep, for their eyes had grown heavy, and they did not know what to answer him.
He came a third time and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest, for the end has come. The hour has arrived, and look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
Come, get up, let us go, for look, the one who will betray me has drawn near.”
While he was still speaking, Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, came, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
The betrayer had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him and lead him away securely.”
And immediately he approached him and said to him, “Rabbi, Rabbi!” And he kissed him.
They laid hands on him and seized him.
One of those standing with him drew a sword, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.
Jesus answered and said to them, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me as though I were a robber?”
“Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple, and you did not arrest me. But this is so that the writings of the prophets may be fulfilled.”
Then all the disciples abandoned him and fled.
A certain young man was following him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body, and the young men seized him.
But he left the linen cloth behind and fled from them naked.
They took Jesus to Caiaphas the high priest, and all the chief priests, scribes, and elders came with him.
Peter followed him at a distance, right into the high priest’s courtyard. He sat with the attendants and warmed himself by the fire.
The chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death, but they found none.
For many gave false testimony against him, but their testimonies did not agree with one another.
Others stood up and gave false testimony against him, saying:
“We heard him say, ‘I will tear down this temple made by human hands, and in three days I will build another, not made by human hands.’”
Yet even then their testimony did not agree.
Then the high priest stood up in their midst and questioned Jesus, saying, “Do you give no answer? What is this testimony they are giving against you?”
But he remained silent and gave no answer. Again the high priest questioned him a second time, saying, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the blessed God?”
Jesus answered and said to him, “You have said that I am. But you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
The high priest immediately tore his robes and said, “What further need do we have of witnesses?”
“Look, you have all heard the blasphemy from his mouth. What do you think?” And they all condemned him as deserving death.
Some began to spit in his face, put a cloth over his head, strike him with their fists, and say, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who is it that struck you?” And the attendants slapped him.
While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest’s servant girls came and saw him warming himself. She looked at him and said:
“You too were with Jesus of Nazareth.”
He denied it and said, “I neither understand nor know what you are saying.” And when he went out into the outer courtyard, a rooster crowed.
The servant girl saw him again and began saying to those standing nearby, “This man too is one of them.” And he denied it again.
A little later, those standing nearby again said to Peter, “You really are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your very speech is like theirs.”
He began to curse and swear, saying, “I do not know the man you are talking about.”
Immediately a rooster crowed a second time, and Peter remembered the words Jesus had said to him: “Before a rooster has crowed twice, you will deny me three times.” And he began to weep.
Immediately in the morning, the chief priests held a consultation with the elders, the scribes, and the whole council. They bound Jesus, took him away, and handed him over to Pilate.
Pilate questioned him, saying, “Are you the king of the Jews?” He answered him, “You say so.”
The chief priests accused him bitterly, but he gave no answer.
Pilate questioned him again: “Do you give no answer? See how many accusations they bring against you.”
But Jesus gave no further answer, so that Pilate was greatly amazed.
Now at the festival he would release to them one prisoner whom they requested.
There was a man named Barabbas, imprisoned with the rebels during whose uprising a man had been killed.
The crowd began shouting loudly and asking him, as was his custom, to release Barabbas for them.
Pilate answered them, “Do you want me to release the king of the Jews for you?”
For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
They also persuaded the crowd to ask him to release Barabbas for them.
Pilate answered them again, “Then what do you want me to do with the king of the Jews?”
Stirred up by the chief priests, they shouted again, “Crucify him!”
Pilate said to them, “What evil has he done?” But they shouted all the more, saying, “Crucify him!”
Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them. After having Jesus flogged, he handed him over to be crucified.
The soldiers took him inside, into the courtyard where the public square was, and called together the whole company.
They dressed him in a red cloak and purple garments, and placed on his head a crown they had made from thorns.
They began greeting him and saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!”
They struck his head with a reed, spat in his face, and knelt down and bowed before him.
When they had mocked him, they stripped off the cloak and the purple garments, dressed him in his own clothes, and led him outside to crucify him.
They detained Simon of Cyrene, who was passing by on his way in from the countryside, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
They brought him to a place called Golgotha, which means “Place of the Skull.”
They offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.
They crucified him and divided his clothes, casting lots over them to determine who would take what.
It was the third hour when they crucified him.
The inscription stating the charge against him read, “He is the king of the Jews.”
They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and one on his left.
And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “He was counted among the lawless.”
And those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, “Ah! You who would tear down the temple and build it in three days,
save yourself and come down from that cross!”
Likewise, the chief priests, mocking him among themselves along with the scribes, said, “He saved others; he cannot save himself.
Let this Christ, this King of Israel, come down now from that cross, so that we may see and believe in him.” And those who had been crucified with him reproached him.
And when the sixth hour came, darkness covered the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said, “Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?” which means, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
And some of those standing around him, when they heard this, said, “He is calling Elijah.”
And someone ran, filled a sponge with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink, saying, “Wait; let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
And Jesus let out a loud cry and gave up his spirit.
And the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
And when the centurion standing there saw that he cried out and gave up his spirit, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God.”
There were also women watching from a distance, among whom were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and Joses, and Salome,
who, when he was in Galilee, followed him and served him, and many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
And when evening came, since it was Friday, leading into the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea came, a respected council member who himself was also awaiting the kingdom of God. He boldly went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
And Pilate was surprised that he had died so soon. He summoned the centurion and questioned him, saying, “Did he really die so soon?”
And when he had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
And Joseph bought linen, took him down, wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a tomb that had been cut out of rock. And he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
But Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Joses saw the place where he was laid.
And when the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome went and prepared spices so that they might come and anoint him.
And early in the morning on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb at sunrise.
And they said to one another, “Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb?”
And looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away from the tomb, for it was very large.
And entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe, and they were alarmed.
And he said to them, “Do not be afraid. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look, here is the place where they laid him.”
But go and tell his disciples and Peter, ‘Look, he is going ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you.’
When they heard this, they went out and fled from the tomb, for they were struck with terror. They said nothing to anyone, because they were afraid.
After rising in the morning on the first day of the week, Jesus appeared to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
She went and told those who had been with him, while they were mourning and weeping.
When they heard that he was alive and had appeared to her, they did not believe.
Later he appeared in another form to those who were going into the countryside.
They went and told the others, but they did not believe either.

Afterward, while the eleven were reclining at table, he appeared to them and rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, because he had appeared to them risen from the dead, and they had not believed.
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to all creation.”
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, and whoever does not believe will be condemned.
These signs will follow those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons and speak in tongues.
They will pick up snakes with their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them at all. They will lay their hands on the sick and heal them.
After speaking with them, the Lord Jesus himself was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of the Father.
They went out and preached throughout the whole earth, with the Lord working with them, and they confirmed the word by all the signs that followed them.
